questions.prompt: In which year did the Titanic sink?

questions.prompt: Who was the first president of the United States?

questions.prompt: Which empire built Machu Picchu?
questions.factOneLiner: The Spanish never found it, which is why so much of it still stands.

questions.prompt: Who was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize?
questions.factOneLiner: She then won a second, in a different science, and is still the only person to do so.

questions.prompt: Which civilisation built the pyramids at Giza?
questions.factOneLiner: The Great Pyramid was the tallest structure on Earth for about 3800 years.

questions.prompt: Who led India's independence movement through nonviolent protest?
questions.factOneLiner: His march to the sea to make salt covered about 380 kilometres.

questions.prompt: Who was Britain's prime minister for most of the Second World War?
questions.factOneLiner: He later won the Nobel Prize in Literature, not Peace.

questions.prompt: Which ship carried the Pilgrims to America in 1620?

questions.prompt: Who discovered penicillin?

questions.prompt: Which country was ruled by shoguns?

questions.prompt: Who was the first person to travel into space?
questions.factOneLiner: His single orbit lasted 108 minutes.

questions.prompt: Who painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel?
questions.factOneLiner: He considered himself a sculptor and took the job reluctantly.

questions.prompt: Which ancient city was buried by Mount Vesuvius?
questions.factOneLiner: The ash preserved loaves of bread still sitting in the ovens.

questions.prompt: Who was the longest reigning British monarch?
questions.factOneLiner: She reigned for just over seventy years.

questions.prompt: What was the name of the first artificial satellite?
questions.factOneLiner: It was a metal sphere the size of a beach ball that simply beeped.

questions.prompt: Which American president gave the Gettysburg Address?
questions.factOneLiner: The whole speech was about two minutes long.

questions.prompt: Which wall was built to keep out northern tribes in Roman Britain?
questions.factOneLiner: It ran about 117 kilometres coast to coast.

questions.prompt: Which document did English barons force King John to seal in 1215?
questions.factOneLiner: Most of its clauses have been repealed, but a few are still law.

questions.prompt: Which two cities were the first targets of atomic weapons?
questions.factOneLiner: The two attacks came three days apart in August 1945.
